land.text: Liaoxi Commandery, 'the Duan held Liaoxi as a ducal fief over their home commandery' (Conquest of the Duan); Wuwuchen 'was based in Liaoxi Commandery' (Duan Wuwuchen)

predecessors.note: Duan Wuwuchen was a Jin vassal: 'petitioned for the imperial court to grant Duan Wuwuchen the title of Duke of Liaoxi' in 307 (the Book of Jin and Zizhi Tongjian place the enfeoffment in 303). The Duan had held the commandery earlier: 'By the Western Jin dynasty, the tribe had grown to 30,000 families'.

land.text: Lingzhi and the cities round it: Zhao 'captured more than forty cities, and Yuyang, Shanggu, and Dai commanderies surrendered'

successors.note: Conquest of the Duan: Lingzhi was the Duan base; Shi Hu entered its palace.

land.text: Liaoxi, whence 'Murong Huang returned to Yan with 5,000 households'

successors.note: The Former Yan dossier's Liaoxi core (Jicheng) was already Murong land from 337; the page does not say who held the Duan's Liaoxi afterwards. Duan Liao fled and was killed in 339.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks: the dukedom of Liaoxi, 'based in Liaoxi Commandery', allied with Wang Jun (You Province) from 303. No area on any page; Cliopatria's Liaoxi region (92,300 km2 in the gazetteer) stands in.

correction.text: 'From Yuyang Commandery to the Liao River' around 321 (Duan tribe infobox): Liaoxi, the Lingzhi country round Tangshan and Yuyang near Beijing

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Wang Jun's fall in 314 the Duan Pidi branch 'seized control of Wang Jun's old capital in Jicheng' and the territory is given as 'From Yuyang Commandery to the Liao River (around 321)'. The extent is the infobox's one line, drawn as Liaoxi plus discs round Tangshan (Lingzhi) and Beijing (Yuyang); Pidi's Jicheng is inside the Beijing disc until 321 (his capture).

region.text: Liaoxi Commandery, 'the Duan held Liaoxi as a ducal fief over their home commandery' (Conquest of the Duan); Wuwuchen 'was based in Liaoxi Commandery' (Duan Wuwuchen)

ledger.note: 307: Duan Wuwuchen made Duke of Liaoxi. The Duan Wuwuchen page dates the title to 307 ('petitioned for the imperial court to grant Duan Wuwuchen the title of Duke of Liaoxi') against 303 in the Book of Jin and Zizhi Tongjian; in 303 Wang Jun had allied with the Duan by marrying his daughter to Wuwuchen.

region.text: Wang Jun's old capital at Jicheng and Yuyang

ledger.note: 314: the Duan take Wang Jun's old capital. 'Wang Jun was defeated by Shi Le in 314'; the Pidi branch 'seized control of Wang Jun's old capital in Jicheng' (Duan tribe page). Wang Jun, Inspector of You Province, is not a state with a dossier. Confidence 2: the year is the page's, the area is a disc round Beijing.

321: Duan Pidi is captured by Later Zhao. 'In 321, Pidi was captured and later killed by Shi Le's state of Later Zhao'. The page gives no land lost; the Beijing disc of Pidi's Jicheng is the researcher's inference (the later-zhao dossier dates the defeat of Pidi 323 and the taking of Shandong from Cao Ni). Confidence 1.

region.text: Lingzhi and the cities north of the Duan capital

ledger.note: January 338: Later Zhao and Former Yan march on the Duan. 'In 338, the Murong, who by now had established the Former Yan, allied with the Later Zhao to destroy the Duan'; the campaign ran 'from January to April 338'; Zhao took Lingzhi, Shi Hu entering its palace (Conquest of the Duan).

region.text: Lingzhi and the cities north of the Duan capital

ledger.note: April 338: the campaign ends in Zhao-Yan victory. 'Zhao captured more than forty cities, and Yuyang, Shanggu, and Dai commanderies surrendered'; Murong Huang returned to Yan with 5,000 households from Liaoxi.

region.text: 'From Yuyang Commandery to the Liao River' around 321 (Duan tribe infobox): Liaoxi, the Lingzhi country round Tangshan and Yuyang near Beijing

ledger.note: 338: the Duan state is destroyed. 'In 338, the Murong ... allied with the Later Zhao to destroy the Duan' (Duan tribe page: 'End of independent rule: 338'); Duan Liao, who fled with over a thousand families, 'sent a messenger from Mount Miyun giving himself up to Shi Hu' in January 339 and was killed for rebelling in 339. The land passed to Later Zhao (Lingzhi and the cities) and Former Yan (Liaoxi); the page does not divide it. Month 4 is the end of the January-April campaign, not a page date.

wars.name: Shi Le's war against Wang Jun and the Duan

zones.text: Wang Jun's old capital at Jicheng

wars.outcome: 'In 313, after some negotiations, Jilujuan agreed with Shi Le to break off relations with Wang Jun'; 'Wang Jun was defeated by Shi Le in 314'; the Pidi branch seized Jicheng.
wars.note: Allied with Wang Jun 303-313; Jilujuan changed sides.

wars.note: The Duan civil war followed Jilujuan's death in 318 (Mobo against Shefuchen and Pidi).

wars.note: The Zhao-Yan alliance broke straight after (Battle of Jicheng, Shi Hu's 100,000 men beaten). [Reviewer ea-03-x: 'to' 339 -> 338, the page's 'January - April 338'; Duan Liao's surrender of January 339 is the aftermath, after the state's end.]

certainty.note: A tribal polity: the page gives a territory in one line ('From Yuyang Commandery to the Liao River') and nothing sharper.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks. Slug duan-liaoxi (ea-03-b's suggestion). Duan Qi (Duan Kan's Shandong state, 350-356) is a separate dossier. The Duan page gives the Duan Wuwuchen title in 307 against 303 (Book of Jin, Zizhi Tongjian); the tribe's rise before the title (the page says the tribe 'had grown to 30,000 families' under the Western Jin) is not dated. No area on any page; the Liaoxi region of the gazetteer and two discs are the reading. Pidi's seat and the order of Pidi, Mobo and Shefuchen between 318 and 325 are tangled in the page's table (Pidi 318-321 and Mobo 318-325 run in parallel). The later-zhao and former-yan dossiers carry no Duan events for 338 (they carry Duan Qi only): both should add a gain from duan-liaoxi in 338 (Lingzhi and the cities for Zhao; Liaoxi's households for Yan) and a contest pair. Gazetteer: all names used exist; Qian'an and Lingzhi are discs round Tangshan.
